text:
### Observed differences

- After A02, the majority continuation flipped: in the earlier window about 58 in 100 of A02's outgoing transitions went to A10 and about 35 went to A07; in the later window about 58 went to A07 and about 39 to A10, and the small share towards A04 (about 4 in 100) was no longer observed. [DIR002]
- After A10 the mix moved the opposite way: earlier, about 60 in 100 of A10's outgoing transitions went to A07 and about 35 returned to A02; later, about 50 returned to A02 and about 38 went to A07. [DIR008]
- More flow was routed into A05: from A04, the share of outgoing transitions going to A05 rose from about 17 to 31 in 100 while the share to A02 fell from about 30 to 17; from A09, the share to A05 rose from about 7 to 16 and to A04 from about 13 to 20, while the share to A03 fell from about 55 to 43. [DIR003, DIR007]
- A05 was executed in more cases: it appeared in about 26 of 100 traces in the earlier window versus about 37 of 100 in the later window (mean occurrences per trace 0.39 vs 0.58); A04 and A06 also appeared somewhat more often (about 28–29 of 100 traces before, about 34 after). [OCC004, OCC003, OCC005]
- A01 and A11 occurred and repeated more within traces: mean occurrences rose from 0.88 to about 1.06 per trace and recurrence support from 0.185 to 0.26, while the share of traces containing them stayed similar (about 65 vs 69 of 100). [OCC001, OCC010]
- Smaller shifts whose sizes are typical of random splitting (empirical strengths about 0.5–0.7): A02, A07 and A10 each appeared in about 28 of 100 traces before versus about 33 after; A08 and A09 occurred slightly more often per trace (0.97 vs 1.05); and the outgoing mixes of A05, A06 and A07 shifted modestly (for example A07 to A11 from about 29 to 19 in 100). [OCC002, OCC006, OCC009, OCC007, OCC008, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the shares between existing alternative paths changed, without activities or paths being added or removed. In the later window, after A02 the direct transition to A07 became the majority continuation (about 58 in 100, previously about 35, with the route via A10 falling from about 58 to 39); after A10, returns to A02 became the plurality (about 50 in 100, previously about 35); and more cases were routed into A05 from A04 (about 17 to 31 in 100) and from A09 (about 7 to 16 in 100), so A05 ran in about 37 of 100 traces after versus about 26 before. Every activity and transition involved was observed with substantial support in both windows and only the shares between alternatives moved, which is the pattern expected when existing paths are taken with different frequencies. [DIR002, DIR008, DIR003, DIR007, OCC004]

Supporting signs: the four routing items show differences larger than in about 98–99 of 100 random re-splits and the A05 participation item about 97 of 100; the increased inflow to A05 agrees with its higher participation; and the rerouting around A02/A10 and around A04/A09 are each internally consistent. [DIR002, DIR008, DIR003, DIR007, OCC004]

Limitations: the evidence set contains no screening expectation, so the number of qualifying items cannot be compared with the number an unchanged process would produce, leaving ordinary sampling variability as a competing explanation that cannot be quantified; several activities also share identical occurrence profiles (A01 with A11, A02 with A07 and A10, A08 with A09), so agreeing items are not independent confirmations; and whether the small A02-to-A04 transition disappeared or only fell below the sampling floor cannot be decided. [OCC001, OCC010, OCC002, OCC006, OCC009, OCC007, OCC008, DIR002]

Other differences: A01 and A11 (and, weakly, A08 and A09) show more repetitions within traces rather than a routing change — mean occurrences and recurrence support rose while trace participation stayed roughly flat. [OCC001, OCC010, OCC007, OCC008]
